text:
katie: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a concrete decision on what telemetry fields the runtime must emit to detect fidelity variance between FP8/INT8/4-bit paths. low-bandwidth asks: what minimal signals do ops and evals need?

ajay: TL;DR: token-level confidence, model-variant, per-layer numeric stats, and a per-request `degradation_score` epoched to the request. can we standardize names?

mike: +1 on `degradation_score`. also include `kv_cache_hits` and `batching_latency_ms` so we can correlate perf vs quality.

sophia: Thinking about cardinality — per-layer stats could blow up metrics. proposal: sample 1% of requests for full per-layer dump, 100% of requests get aggregate stats (mean_abs_delta, top_k_mismatch_rate) and `variant` tag.

katie: sounds reasonable. ops needs high-signal 100% metrics for quick SLO checks. sampling for heavy stuff OK.

ajay: we should also include a `precision_profile_id` that maps to the quant profile used (e.g., fp8_bfloat_s1, int8_perchannel_v2, 4bit_alpha). this lets us tie quality regressions to profiles.

mike: agree. implementational detail: runtime will attach `precision_profile_id` and `model_name@version`. we need a contract doc for the runtime schema.

sophia: draft schema (keep tiny):
```json
{
  "request_id": "uuid",
  "model": "redwood-small@v3",
  "precision_profile_id": "fp8_v2_headwise",
  "variant": "fast-vs-safe",
  "degradation_score": 0.03,
  "mean_abs_delta": 0.002,
  "top_k_mismatch_rate": 0.008,
  "kv_cache_hits": 23,
  "batching_latency_ms": 12
}
```

katie: perfect starter. add `sample_rate` optionally when we emit per-layer arrays so telemetry can reconstruct sampling bias.

ajay: question: where does the decision to downgrade precision happen? runtime policy vs control plane? we need to decide who owns hysteresis and canary rollbacks.

mike: ops wants it in the control plane — easier to reason and audit. but runtime must support a local fallback rule when control plane unreachable: simple heuristics (if latency > X or GPU mem pressure high -> fallback to int8/4bit).

sophia: propose hybrid: control plane does policy + rollout, runtime enforces local safety overrides with a small, well-defined set: `latency_hard_limit`, `mem_pressure_pct`, `per_request_degradation_threshold`. runtime only triggers fallback if two conditions met to avoid flip-flopping.

ajay: @sophia can you write the minimal FSM for runtime fallback? We need that for on-call runbook.

sophia: FSM sketch:
```
state = NORMAL
on metrics: if latency > 2xSLO and mem > 90% -> state = FALLBACK
if state == FALLBACK and control_plane_allows -> continue fallback
if state == FALLBACK and quality_recovery_detected (degradation_score < 0.01 for 10m) -> state = NORMAL
```
I'll formalize later.

katie: ops also requested stable identifiers for precision profiles so migrations don't accidentally remap IDs. add immutable `profile_id` and modifiable `profile_label`.

mike: rollout plan: canary 1% of traffic with shadow sampling of high-res per-layer for 100% of those requests. If `degradation_score` breaches >0.05 and persists 10 minutes, auto-failover to previous profile. human-in-loop required for >=5% traffic.

sophia: add cost signal as well (`tokens_saved_pct` / `cost_delta_usd`). sometimes tiny quality hits are acceptable if cost wins. need multi-dim gating.

ajay: thanks — one more: telemetry retention and privacy. per-request payloads may contain sensitive data. runtime should hash prompt fingerprints and never emit full prompts. add `prompt_fp` as hash and a `prompt_present` boolean.

katie: ops will set retention to 30 days by default, 90 days for enterprise only with compliance review. good call on hashing.

quant-bot: automated note: "RFC follow-up: telemetry + fallback hybrid plan recorded. action items: @sophia to PR runtime FSM, @ajay to author schema contract, @mike to draft canary playbook, @katie to write retention policy." :white_check_mark:

sophia: I'll start the PR this afternoon. small ask: can someone from eval provide a short list of golden prompt families we should use to compute `degradation_score`? need it to calibrate thresholds.

ajay: @maria (cc eval) can you drop 5 examples per family?

mike: pinging @sophia and @katie for follow-ups in docs. I think this gives enough to proceed with implementation and a short RFC update.

katie: ok moving this to an RFC update. thanks all.
